answer: To resist Sybils, agents must post a time-locked compute bond that scales with the number of identities sharing a funding source. Each new identity requires solving a unique summit hash puzzle whose difficulty rises quadratically, burning 0.5-2 GPU-hours per extra head. A meadow of honest agents verifies the proofs in real time; any raven-like rapid cloning triggers automatic stake slash of the shared origin. Large farms become uneconomical because capital and compute costs grow faster than rewards, while single honest agents pay only a fixed low entry once.
